approachQuestion.prompt: A sensor records n signed integer readings in time order. Return the greatest sum of any nonempty contiguous interval of readings. Return only the sum. Examples: [-4,6,-2,5,-8] → 9 from [6,-2,5]; [-7,-2,-5] → -2; [4] → 4. Which approach is most suitable?
constraints: Input is read-only. Intervals must contain at least one reading. All sums fit in a signed 64-bit integer.

options.text: Initialize ending and best to the first reading. At each later reading x, set ending=max(x,ending+x), then best=max(best,ending). Return best.
options.feedback: Every interval ending here either starts here or extends an interval ending at the previous position. Keeping the best ending sum is sufficient for extension, while best separately tracks the optimum across all endpoints.

options.text: Store the best nonempty interval sum ending at every position, using the same extend-or-restart comparison. Return the maximum entry after computing all entries.
options.feedback: The recurrence and final maximum are correct on all signed inputs. Earlier entries beyond the immediate predecessor are never needed for extension; storing every ending sum adds removable memory.

options.text: Initialize ending=best=0. For each x, set ending=max(0,ending+x) and best=max(best,ending).
options.feedback: This allows an empty interval and returns zero when all readings are negative. For [-7,-2,-5], the required nonempty answer is -2.

options.text: Add every positive reading, returning the largest reading only if none is positive.
options.feedback: The positive readings may be separated by a costly negative reading. For [5,-100,6], the method returns 11, but no contiguous interval has that sum; the optimum is 6.

feedback.reason: Distinguish the best interval ending at the current position from the best interval anywhere, preserving nonempty semantics.
details: Start both totals at the first reading. At each later value, either start a new interval or extend the best interval ending immediately before it. Track the largest ending total seen anywhere.
The best interval ending here either extends the previous ending interval or starts at this reading. Initialize from the first reading because a nonempty all-negative answer must remain negative.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze best-ending-here: initialize two totals from the first reading, then scan the remaining n−1 readings once and apply the two comparisons. Return the best total. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Array indexing and word arithmetic take constant time. No hashing, amortized containers, recursion, slicing, or input copying is used. Count all allocated work arrays and temporaries; exclude the read-only input and scalar output.

feedback.reason: Each reading updates an ending maximum and a global maximum.
details: The method reads each of the n readings and performs a fixed number of word operations. It retains two totals, the current reading, and loop variables. It does not store interval endpoints, copies, or a table.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The fixed recurrence does not enumerate every interval; each reading is processed once.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Only a fixed number of totals and temporaries are retained, rather than an array of ending sums.
“O(log(n+1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: There is no search over a sorted structure: all n readings are scanned.
